To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the δ13C values of lacustrine carbonates in the Koobi Fora sequence record the varying proportions of carbon from metabolic and atmospheric reservoirs, and that the δ18O values indicate that the isotopically lightest water in the lake was present in the Pliocene, and the isotopically heaviest water in the lake has been in the Holocene.

the stable isotopic composition of carbonates in sediments of the Turkana Basin record the paleohydrology and paleoclimatology of the basin, and that the isotopic record indicates a period of major environmental instability from about 1.9 to about 1.5 myr ago, followed by the present arid and hot conditions.
the stable isotopic composition of carbonates in the Plio-Pleistoecne and Recent sediments in Lake Turkana Basin provide constraints on paleoenvironmental conditions in this region.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the use of isotopic analyses of sediments to reconstruct the history of a fluvio-lacustrine basin.
the use of isotopic data to reconstruct the paleohydrology of a Plio-Plestiocene fluvial-lakustrine system in East Africa.
the use of stable isotopic analyses of carbonates to determine the history of a fluvio-lacustrine depositional system in the Turkana Basin of Kenya.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the isotopic data from the Koobi Fora sediments provide a record of paleoenvironmental changes in the Turkana Basin during the past 4.5 myr, and that the data indicate that the basin has been subject to climatic instability throughout that interval.
the paleoenvironment of the Turkana Basin has not been as hot and arid as at present during the past 4 million years.
the Plio-Pleisocene sediments of the basin record a history of climatic instability and that the present conditions represent a maximum of the range of climatic variation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the isotopic data for the Plio-Plestocene sequence are consistent with a history of alternating arid and wet conditions, and that the present climate is as hot and as dry as any during the Plio-Plestocene.

the Pliocene sediments were deposited in a relatively wet environment, that the Pleistocene sediments were laid down in a relatively dry environment, that the present conditions in this part of East Africa are as dry and hot as they had been at any time in the past 4 myr, and that the present environment is not as dry and hot in the basin as it had been during deposition of the Plio-Pleisocene sediments.
the isotopic data from this study are consistent with other paleoenvironmental evidence from the basin and with the paleoclimate history inferred from the marine record.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the stable isotopic composition of carbonates in fluvial-lake sequences can provide a wealth of information on the paleohydrological and paleoclimatic conditions in the past.
the δ13C values in lacustrine carbonates are not reliable paleotemperature proxies in this setting because they are controlled by the relative proportions of atmospheric CO2 and metabolic CO2.
the isotopic signatures of the carbonates in the Koobi Fora sequence are consistent with the paleoclimatic and paleoecological interpretations that have been made from this sequence.
